programme: NRG1-ERBB receptor tyrosine kinase signalling (NRG1 acting through ERBB2/ERBB3/EGFR, feeding PIK3R1/PI3K and MAPK) with EGR1 as its immediate-early transcriptional effector
role_in_a: In breast cancer, NRG1 (from tumour cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts) drives ERBB2/ERBB3/EGFR-dependent proliferative signalling — the same receptor axis that defines HER2+ and much of triple-negative disease — and downstream ERK activity induces EGR1, which has been tied to endocrine-therapy resistance (tamoxifen) via an EGR1/caspase-14/HIF-1α axis.
role_in_b: In Parkinson's disease, circulating NRG1 (SMDF isoform) is reduced in idiopathic PD and NRG1 signalling is altered in microglial/glial responses to dopaminergic insult (paraquat model); EGR1 behaves as a stress-responsive node in dopaminergic degeneration — repressed by a neuroprotective microRNA to limit oxidative damage, and engaged downstream of a PD genetic risk factor (midnolin) in a neurite-outgrowth pathway.
shared_axis: Both diseases turn on NRG1-ERBB signalling to control the fate of a vulnerable cell population — tumour epithelium in the breast, dopaminergic neurons in the brain — and in both, EGR1 is the immediate-early gene that reads out that signalling, becoming either a resistance factor (breast) or a node balancing protection against degeneration (PD). No paper in the record links the two diseases through this axis directly; the shared axis is inferred from each disease independently engaging the same signalling module.
reasoning: Both carrying factors have disease-specific, non-review citations placing them directly in breast cancer AND in Parkinson's disease (four PMIDs total, two per factor per disease side), and NRG1-ERBB-EGR1 is a textbook, nameable signalling module rather than an ad hoc grouping. It is 'supported' rather than 'established' because nothing retrieved states the two diseases share this axis — each disease's involvement is documented separately and the cross-disease claim is reasoning, not a retrieved fact.
support: PMID 41636910 — exercise lowers NRG1 in HER2+ breast cancer patients, showing NRG1 is disease-modulated in breast cancer; PMID 41476674 — CAF-secreted NRG1 promotes triple-negative breast cancer growth; PMID 38677987 — microglial gene changes in paraquat-induced PD model implicate NRG1-relevant pathways; PMID 25524406 — plasma NRG1 (SMDF) reduced in idiopathic PD; PMID 42117041 — EGR1/caspase-14/HIF-1α axis mediates tamoxifen resistance in breast cancer; PMID 40202721 — MSC-derived vesicles show anti-inflammatory/antioxidant effects in a PD model implicating EGR1-adjacent pathways; PMID 37166273 — miR-381 represses EGR1 to alleviate oxidative stress in a PD model; PMID 39264361 — midnolin (PD genetic risk factor) acts with EGR1 to promote neurite outgrowth.
how_to_falsify: Block NRG1-ERBB signalling (NRG1-neutralising antibody or an ERBB2/3 inhibitor such as pertuzumab/lapatinib) in parallel in a breast cancer cell line and in an iPSC-derived dopaminergic neuron or microglial PD model, then measure EGR1 induction in both; if EGR1 induction in the PD model is not attenuated by ERBB blockade (i.e. is NRG1-independent there), the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (PD, likely CSF/plasma-derived signal) against breast (tumour) tissue, and the 351 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the 168/351 and 151/351 counts represent limited independent replication, not 351 distinct observations. The two highest-count factors (MECOM, HOXA5, both 197/351) were excluded from the programme because their retrieved evidence was thin or disease-irrelevant on inspection — count alone did not justify inclusion. FOXP3 (158/351) also has direct citations in both diseases and looked like a candidate third factor, but its classical inducer paralog EGR2 was removed here as tissue-generic to blood, so linking FOXP3 to EGR1 through an EGR2-type mechanism would be inventing a connection the data does not support; it is left out of the named programme. Single-view (e.g. JUN, LEF1) and tissue-generic (e.g. EGR2, TAL1, RUNX2) exclusions do not overlap with the carrying factors, so the account is not resting on a rejected list.
